title: Turtle Tower
visualBrief: Hanoi’s small lake monument with a raised base and entrance steps, two diminishing open Gothic arcades, recessed pilasters, brick terrace infill, narrow stone balustrades, east-facing circular aperture, relief medallions and a curled Vietnamese roof. Continuous deterministic vertex tints reproduce weathered plaster without copied image textures.

nativeAxes.front: Native +Z faces east toward the third-floor circular opening and inscription; +X points north
nativeAxes.origin: Center of the exact mapped monument footprint, Y=0 at the grass island ground

scaleBasis: Municipal tourism documentation gives the height, base rise, three shrinking floor plans, square top and east round aperture. The exact map outline agrees within centimetres. Its four close on-island photographs establish unequal pointed openings, recessed surrounds, stairs, weathering, brick infill and balustrades. The national tourism brochure page 7 establishes the complete roof and scroll silhouette. Intermediate elevations and fine plaster relief are proportionally reconstructed.

geographicProposal.evidence: Exact Q1134533 way178995269 agrees with the published 6.28 by 4.54 m footprint. Hanoi tourism describes the third-floor circular 0.68 m opening and inscription on the east facade. Native +Z is this east-facing long elevation and +X points north. The documented island ground is the base datum; the surrounding lake and grass island remain mapped terrain.
geographicProposal.limitations: The small island and lake are host terrain/water, not part of this monument mesh. Island ground contact requires terrain data to retain the island instead of generalizing it into water.

geometrySource: Original deterministic geometry informed by cited dimensions, measured plans and photographs. No downloaded mesh or photographic texture is embedded.
sourceLicense: Original geometry under repository license. Map-derived outline information is attributed to OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications retain their own rights.
materialMethod: Shared material graphs with metric repeat UV0 and original vertex tints; GLB PBR fallback remains self-contained. No per-model texture duplication.
limitations: The monument follows the retained mapped footprint and east-facing circular aperture. Host terrain/water must retain its small island; no new lake-level or island-contact survey is claimed.
Intermediate heights and fine roof relief remain proportional reconstructions. Inscription fields and medallions preserve layout without copied calligraphy or heraldic artwork.

Dense weathered masters are preserved. Browser plaster uses shared textures and quiet material colors; exact stains, tiny fittings and guard/scroll density aggregate. Interiors, transient vegetation and maintenance equipment remain excluded. Physical-device timing is pending.
reviewStatus: medium-fi; current hash-bound visual acceptance recorded in qa.json

appearance.identity: Raised8.8m Hanoi lake monument: attached east steps, two shrinking open pointed arcades with ten unequal bays each, pilasters and cornices, brick lower parapet, stone upper balustrade, east circular aperture/plaque, relief medallions and four curled roof tips with paired scrolls.
appearance.master: Preserve the269320triangle dense weathered source and imported master unchanged.
appearance.browser: Four complete source-local levels preserve the20 arcade openings, east round aperture and whole roof. Shared low-frequency plaster replaces dense weathering tessellation; inner walls use the same physical plaster tint and runtime lighting. Skyline uses coarse curls/scrolls and guard cards. District restores inner gallery faces, bowed gables and roof scrolls; street/closeup restore finer relief, balusters and lights.
